liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Althea** (2 reviews): Bass plunges stand out in this version; Reviewer calls the first-set Althea a killer [8][10]
- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Opener is called mean and hard-hitting [10]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Playin' into Uncle John's Band is described as dreamlike [14]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drums end with a wild polyrhythmic jam, recommended on headphones, leading into the Spanish theme [9]
- **Spanish Jam** (1 review): Reviewer uses this Spanish theme on an answering machine, shortened because others found it too long [13]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-04-07.135528.sbd-pc.miller.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 152 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [1]
- **gd84-04-07.sbd.dodd.13816.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 149 min; rated 3.62/5 by 13 [3]. Said about its sound: Pitch warble runs through every track of this soundboard copy, with instruments drifting out of tune; reviewer found it unlistenable; Apart from the warble, second set sounds clean; bass is prominent and the drummers sound punchy; Decent taper-style soundboard session; Bobby sounds slightly off, otherwise good quality [6][8][11]
- **gd1984-04-07.108618.Beyer-DaWeez.D5scott.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 149 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording by DaWeez sounds excellent, livelier than the rather dry 1984 soundboard [15]
- **gd1984-04-07.146012.sbd.GEMS.flac1648**: soundboard; 21 songs; 159 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- Wharf Rat sits in the post-Other One slot, with transitions smooth yet tight; reviewer likes the Saturday encore-slot song [10]
- Reviewer attended; the show came the night after Las Vegas on a southwestern tour [11]
- Second set is described as soaring, with each tune building; Healy's usual weirdness audible in the mix [9]
- Called the meltiest second set the reviewer has heard, with Bob playing very far out [14]
- Reviewer suggests the Philly run that spring as further good 1984 listening [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-04-07.135528.sbd-pc.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Dat -> CD (shnid=13816) [1]. Also: Soundboard transfer was pitch-corrected, with help from Joe B. Jones [1]
- **gd84-04-07.sbd.dodd.13816.sbeok.shnf**: source: sbd>MC>Dat>cdEac >cool edit > shntool > cdwav >shnv3Eac >shn (secure with proper offsets) by Ernie Dodd [3]
- **gd1984-04-07.108618.Beyer-DaWeez.D5scott.flac16**: taped by DaWeez; transferred by D5scott; source: source: 3 Beyer M160's > Nak100 > Sony TC-D5M - 17th Row Center - analog master cassettes - TDK MA-R90's [4]. Also: Only audience source for this date on the archive; taped by DaWeez with Beyer mics, transferred by D5scott [15]
- **gd1984-04-07.146012.sbd.GEMS.flac1648**: taped by Jeff Knudson; transferred by Jay Haines, Jason Chastain, Jamie Waddell; source: Soundboard Master from The Knudsen Collection at Lossless Legs The cassettes were donated to www.shnflac.net by Jeff Knudsen in 2018. [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Irvine Meadows Amphitheatre - April 7, 1984](https://www.dead.net/show/april-7-1984) [18]
